title: Daemon-resident DD engine with incremental updates
description: DD engine is created and destroyed on every sutra_review call. PRD specifies lazy-populated, daemon-resident DD with incremental updates and idle eviction.\n\nHold Option<DdEngine> per workspace in daemon state. Ingest on first DD query, update on incremental parse, evict after dd_idle_timeout_sec (config field already exists but is dead). Review compositor borrows shared engine.

acceptance_criteria.text: DD engine persists across sutra_review calls for the same workspace
Incremental parse triggers engine.update() with delta edges
Engine evicted after dd_idle_timeout_sec idle period
dd_idle_timeout_sec config field is wired up
Review results identical to per-call creation

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review (c480f64..390462c):

Verdict: needs-attention

[high] Shared DD engine can ignore fresh DB edges after concurrent reparse (src/tools/review.rs:120-128). build_findings reads current db.import_edges() but when shared engine is already loaded it discards those edges and queries old in-memory graph. Reparse invalidation removes map entry but can't invalidate Arc<DdEngine> already handed to in-flight sutra_review. Violates requirement that shared-engine results remain identical to per-call creation.

[medium] Idle eviction leaves cached engine resident indefinitely (src/daemon.rs:278-285). Scheduler logs eviction when evict_if_idle() returns true but never removes the map entry. DdEngine::evict_if_idle preserves the full edge list (Warm->Loaded), and Loaded engines are never eligible for eviction. dd_idle_timeout_sec does not bound daemon memory as required.

Recommendation: On idle timeout, remove workspace entry from dd_engines or add true unload state. Add test that daemon cache drops idle workspace after configured timeout.
